name: vzt-paste-image
displayName: VZT: Paste & Drop Files into Terminal
description: Drag a zip, PDF, doc or screenshot anywhere onto the editor area — or Cmd+V a file or screenshot — and its path lands on the prompt line of the Claude Code session in the integrated terminal. Falls through to normal text paste otherwise.

configuration.title: VZT: Paste & Drop Files into Terminal

vzt.pasteImage.captureDroppedImages.description: Forward dropped IMAGES (png, jpg, gif, webp, bmp) to the terminal. The image is copied to ~/.vzt/shots first, because the macOS screenshot temp path does not survive. Only acts when a terminal is open.

vzt.pasteImage.captureDroppedFiles.description: Forward dropped ARCHIVES, DOCUMENTS and MEDIA (zip, tar, pdf, docx, xlsx, csv, mp4, …) to the terminal. These are types you would not open in VS Code on purpose, so opening one is almost always a drop that missed the terminal. The original path is sent — nothing is copied.

vzt.pasteImage.captureDroppedFilesOutsid.description: Forward any OTHER file type, but only when it lives outside your open workspace folders. This is what makes dragging ~/Downloads/notes.md work without hijacking every project file you open. Turn it off if a file outside the workspace ever gets forwarded when you meant to read it.

vzt.pasteImage.pasteClipboardFiles.description: Cmd+V in the terminal pastes the PATH of a file copied in Finder. Only reached when the clipboard holds no text, so ordinary pasting is unaffected.

commands.title: VZT: Paste File, Image or Text into Terminal
